name: Universal RAG
tagline: Agentic RAG search over SharePoint and local Office documents, PDFs and emails, with cited answers.
problem: Corporate knowledge sits in SharePoint folders full of PowerPoint decks, spreadsheets, Word files, PDFs and email archives, and finding a specific figure means opening files one by one. Universal RAG indexes those folders and answers plain-English questions with the file, page, slide or sheet each answer came from. It is built to run on a work laptop with Python only, without Docker.
how: Point it at a SharePoint folder path or a local folder and give the collection a name.
Parsers extract text from PowerPoint (with OCR on slide images), Excel, Word, PDF and email files, keeping page, slide and sheet numbers.
Text is split into 800-character chunks with 200 overlap, embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large and stored in ChromaDB; MD5 hashes skip files that have not changed.
When you ask a question, an LLM first analyses it for intent, folders, file types and the kind of answer needed.
The agent retrieves the top matching chunks, optionally filtered by folder or file type, and generates an answer from that evidence with a confidence level.
Results can be exported to a three-sheet Excel workbook (Summary, Sources, Evidence) or sent through Outlook.
features: Next.js interface with Index Documents and Ask Questions tabs, plus a single-file HTML interface for zero-install use.
Folder and file-type filters (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, PDF, Email) on queries.
Separate named collections for different document sets.
Evidence display with file name, file path, SharePoint link, page or slide number and relevance score.
Model presets endpoint: best accuracy, balanced and cost effective.
Support for Azure OpenAI as well as OpenAI.
ai: An LLM (GPT-4 Turbo by default) analyses each query and returns intent, folder and file type hints, and a refined query as JSON.
OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embeds document chunks for semantic retrieval in ChromaDB.
The same LLM writes the final answer from the retrieved evidence and cites the sources it used.
Tesseract OCR extracts text from images inside PowerPoint slides before embedding.

stack.frontend: Next.js 14, React 18, Tailwind CSS, lucide-react; standalone HTML UI
stack.data: ChromaDB vector store, FAISS, JSON index state
stack.ai: OpenAI or Azure OpenAI (GPT-4 Turbo, text-embedding-3-large), Tesseract OCR
stack.deploy: Local Python launcher and Windows batch file, Docker Compose

run:
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
# add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env
python backend/main.py  # API on :8000, then open simple_ui.html
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev  # optional Next.js UI
notes: Ran locally: FastAPI backend (uvicorn backend.main:app) and the Next.js frontend in dev mode, plus simple_ui.html served statically, all on capture ports. The backend imports win32com for Outlook at startup, which only exists on Windows, so a stub module was put on PYTHONPATH outside the repo; Outlook email does not work on Linux. pywin32 was left out of the install. No OpenAI key was available and the repo has no mock or offline mode, so no documents were indexed and no answers were generated; the screens show the real input forms, filters and API with no answer or evidence views. SharePoint is not configured, so the health check reports it as disconnected and no folder list appears. The model recommendations screen is real output from the running API.
